arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: General Dreeben argued the warrant particularly described the place and things to be seized.
Mr. Reichel noted that triggering events are commonly not so clean.
Justice Kennedy suggested that adding a qualification makes a big change in warrant usage.
Justice Souter emphasized an ongoing obligation of reasonableness in how searches are carried out.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case examines the validity of anticipatory search warrants. The government argues these warrants are legal if probable cause exists at issuance. The defendant argues execution requires a specific triggering event to occur first.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the limits of anticipatory search warrants. It determines when police may enter a home. It balances privacy rights against law enforcement needs. It sets a standard for future warrant executions.
